Prealgebra · Lesson 3.1

Factors and Multiples

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A factor of a number is a whole number that divides it with nothing left over. Picture it as a side of a rectangle with that area. Each factor has a partner, the matching side, and the two multiply to the original number.

Problem
A class arranges 24 floor cushions into one full rectangular block, every row the same length, no cushion left over. How many different row counts work?
Show a hint
  • A number of rows works only if you can split 24 into that many equal rows with nothing left over. Try 1 row, then 2, then 3, and keep going, checking each time whether 24 divides up cleanly.
Show the full solution
Pair each row count with the row length it forces. 1×24,2×12,3×8,4×61×24,2×12,3×8,4×6 Both numbers in every pair work as a row count, so the full list is 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 241, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, which is 88​ of them. These are the factors, or divisors, of 24, the numbers that divide it with nothing left over. They come two at a time because each side of a rectangle fixes the opposite side.
Problem
Find all the factors of 48 by writing factor pairs 1×48,2×24,…1×48,2×24,… and stopping once the two sides of a pair would cross. How many factors does 48 have?
Show a hint
  • The moment you find a small side like 3, the matching side is forced, since 3 rows must each be 48÷348÷3 tiles long. So every small factor you find hands you a large one for free.
  • Watch the two sides of each pair close in on each other. Once the next side you would test is bigger than the partner it would pair with, every grid past that point is just one you have already seen turned on its side.
Show the full solution
Climb from 1, writing each factor beside the partner it forces. 1×48,2×24,3×16,4×12,6×81×48,2×24,3×16,4×12,6×8 Reading both numbers out of every pair gives 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 481, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, which is 1010​ factors. You stop after 6 because the next divisor, 8, is already standing on the right of 6×86×8. Once the number you are about to test would be larger than its own partner, every rectangle has already turned up, just mirrored.

If 66 is a factor of 3636, then 3636 is a multiple of 66. Count by sixes, 6,12,18,24,30,366,12,18,24,30,36, and you land on 3636 after six steps. Factor and multiple are one relationship read from its two ends.

Problem
A train starts at stone 0 and rolls forward exactly 7 stones at a time. How many of the four stones 28, 35, 50, 63 does it land on?
Show a hint
  • Keep adding 77. 7,14,21,28,35,42,49,56,637,14,21,28,35,42,49,56,63. Which of the four stones appear on that list?
Show the full solution
Count by sevens. 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 637, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63. Stones 28, 35, and 63 all appear, and 50 does not, since the train steps from 49 straight to 56. That is 33​ stones. Each landing reads two ways. 77 is a factor of 28 because 28=4×728=4×7, and 28 is a multiple of 7 because it sits four 7-steps out from 0.
Problem
For each pair, decide whether the first number is a factor of the second, a multiple of it, both, or neither. (a) 4 and 12 (b) 15 and 5 (c) 8 and 8 (d) 6 and 9. In how many of the four pairs is the first number a factor of the second?
Show a hint
  • For each pair ask two separate questions. Does the first number divide the second evenly, and is the first number itself a whole number times the second?
  • aa is a factor of bb when b=a×(whole number)b=a×(whole number). Check the pair where both numbers are equal carefully.
Show the full solution
(a) 12=4×312=4×3, so 4 is a factor of 12. (b) 15 does not divide 5, so 15 is a multiple of 5 rather than a factor. (c) 8=8×18=8×1, so 8 is both a factor and a multiple of itself. (d) 6 does not divide 9 evenly, so neither. Only (a) and (c) qualify, giving 22​ pairs. Parts (a) and (b) are the same fact told from opposite ends, and (c) shows every number is both a factor and a multiple of itself.
Key idea
Factor and multiple describe the same relationship. A whole number ff is a factor (or divisor) of nn when n=f×kn=f×k for some whole number kk. Equivalently, n÷fn÷f leaves no remainder. As a picture, nn objects fill a rectangle with ff along one side. Stated the other way, nn is a multiple of ff, which is kk whole steps of size ff from 00. So ff is a factor of nn exactly when nn is a multiple of ff. Factors come in pairs, since ff is matched by n÷fn÷f, and the two multiply to nn.
Problem
The factors of 36 pair up as 1×36, 2×18, 3×12, 4×9, 6×61×36, 2×18, 3×12, 4×9, 6×6, nine factors in all. How many factors does 49 have?
Show a hint
  • Every pair so far used two different side lengths. Look hard at 6×66×6, and note that 49=7×749=7×7.
  • List every whole number that divides 49 evenly.
Show the full solution
The pairs are 1×491×49 and 7×77×7, and the second adds only one new factor because 7 is its own partner. The factors are 1, 7, 491, 7, 49, so 49 has 33​. Factors normally arrive two at a time, so a count is even unless one factor pairs with itself, which happens exactly for perfect squares. That is why 36 and 49 come out odd while 35, splitting only as 1×351×35 and 5×75×7, has four.
Key idea
A whole number has an odd number of factors exactly when it is a perfect square. Almost every factor pairs with a different partner, so factors come two at a time and the count is even. The one way to break that is for a factor to pair with itself, f×f=nf×f=n, which happens exactly when nn is a perfect square. That self-paired factor is counted once, so the total is odd. The unpaired factor is the side of the square.
Problem
Priya lists every factor of 20, and Owen lists every multiple of 20. Only one of them can ever finish. How many numbers are on that finished list?
Show a hint
  • A factor of 20 is a side of a rectangle with area 20, so no factor can be longer than 20. Owen's list has no such ceiling.
  • Hunt the factors in pairs, 1×201×20, 2×102×10, 4×54×5.
Show the full solution
Priya is the one who finishes, since no factor of 20 can be bigger than 20 itself. Hunting in pairs gives 1×201×20, 2×102×10, 4×54×5, so her list is 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 201, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, which is 66​ numbers. Owen never finishes, because from any multiple he can always take one more step of 20. Note that 20 sits on both lists, as its own largest factor and its own smallest positive multiple.
Problem
A lighthouse flashes every 8th second. How many flashes fall in the range 100 through 250 inclusive?
Show a hint
  • The flashes happen exactly at the multiples of 88. Count every multiple of 88 up to 250250, then peel off the ones that fall below 100100.
  • To count multiples of 88 up to a number, see how many whole steps of 88 fit inside it. For 250250, how many times does 88 go in?
Show the full solution
The flashes sit at the multiples of 8. Up to 250, the largest is 248=31×8248=31×8, since 32×8=25632×8=256 overshoots, so 31 multiples fit. Below 100, the largest is 96=12×896=12×8, so 12 fall short of the window. Subtracting leaves 31−12=1931−12=19​ Counting to the top and removing everything under the bottom beats listing them all. Check the endpoints though, since an endpoint that is itself a multiple has to be counted.
Key idea
Factors are finite, multiples are not. Every factor of nn is at least 11 and at most nn, since its partner side is never smaller than 11. Only finitely many numbers fit in that range. But from any multiple you can step once more to a new one, so multiples never run out. Three smaller facts hold. 11 is a factor of every nn, every nn is both a factor and a multiple of itself, and 00 is a multiple of every nn. To count the multiples of nn from 11 up to a value VV, count how many whole nn-steps fit. That count is V÷nV÷n with the remainder dropped. Within a range, count up to the top and subtract the multiples below the bottom. Check whether each endpoint is itself a multiple.

Now picture two multiples of nn added or subtracted. The shared factor nn can be pulled out, so the result is still a multiple of nn. But add a non-multiple to a multiple and the result is never a multiple.

Problem
A machine dispenses and swallows tokens only in packs of 9. Starting at 0, a player receives 153, then 72 more, then returns 18. Find the final count, and explain why it must be a multiple of 9.
Show a hint
  • Every amount the machine moves is a whole number of 99s. Write each of 153153, 7272, and 1818 as 99 times something, then collect the 99s.
  • If three amounts are 9×179×17, 9×89×8, and 9×29×2, what happens when you pull the 99 out in front of the whole calculation?
Show the full solution
The straight count is 153+72−18=207153+72−18=207. Every amount is a whole number of 9s, 153=9×17153=9×17, 72=9×872=9×8, and 18=9×218=9×2, so the total is 9×17+9×8−9×2=9×(17+8−2)=9×23=207.9×17+9×8−9×2=9×(17+8−2)=9×23=207​. The 9 is a shared factor of every piece, so it slides out front and leaves a whole number behind. Adding or subtracting whole numbers of 9s can only ever build another whole number of 9s.
Problem
A turnstile reads 240, a multiple of 12. A glitch adds 17. Explain why 240 + 17 cannot be a multiple of 12, then find the smallest positive number to add to restore a multiple of 12.
Show a hint
  • Suppose 240+17240+17 were a multiple of 1212. Then 1717 would be the difference of two multiples of 1212. What does the previous problem say such a difference has to be?
  • The new count is 257257. Find the next multiple of 1212 above it, then see how far away it sits.
Show the full solution
240+17=257240+17=257. Since 12×21=25212×21=252 and 12×22=26412×22=264, the count 257 sits between two multiples of 12 and is not one, so the next marker is 264 and you must add 264−257=7.264−257=7​. It could never have been a multiple, because if it were, the difference 257−240=17257−240=17 would have to be a multiple of 12 as well. The stray 17 is 5 past a multiple of 12, which is exactly why 7 more gets you back.
Problem
Envelope AA holds a multiple of 8 dollars and envelope BB holds a multiple of 8 dollars, so the two can never total exactly 250 dollars. What is the closest total they can reach?
Show a hint
  • By closure, what kind of number is A+BA+B forced to be, whatever AA and BB are?
  • Compare 250 with 8×318×31 and 8×328×32.
Show the full solution
Both envelopes hold multiples of 8, so the total is a multiple of 8 as well. Since 8×31=2488×31=248 and 8×32=2568×32=256, the total skips straight past 250, and the closest it can come is 248248​, for instance with A=240A=240 and B=8B=8. Closure settled the question without either amount ever being known.

The number 1212 is built from 33 and 44, since 12=4×312=4×3. So is every multiple of 1212 also a multiple of 33, and of 44? And does it work the other way? Is every multiple of 33 a multiple of 1212?

Key idea
Two rules for when a number is a multiple. The first is closure. Add or subtract two multiples of nn and the result is a multiple of nn again, since the shared nn factors out, na±nb=n(a±b)na±nb=n(a±b). A multiple of nn plus a non-multiple is never a multiple, since subtracting the multiple back off would make the other number a multiple too. The second is chaining. If aa is a factor of bb, then every multiple of bb is also a multiple of aa, since that multiple has bb as a factor and bb has aa as a factor. A multiple of 1212 is therefore a multiple of 1,2,3,4,61,2,3,4,6 as well. Chaining works only toward smaller factors, so a multiple of 33 need not be a multiple of 1212.
Problem
A workshop packs beeswax sheets in bundles of 12, and 12=4×312=4×3, so any whole number of bundles holds a number of sheets that is a multiple of 3 and of 4. The reverse does not follow. Among the multiples of 3 from 3 through 60, how many are not multiples of 12?
Show a hint
  • Every bundle already splits into groups of 3, so a stack of bundles does too. The question runs the other way. Count 3, 6, 9, 12, and on up to 60, and mark which of those land exactly on a whole number of bundles.
  • Instead of testing each multiple of 3 one at a time, count how many multiples of 3 sit in the range, then count the multiples of 12 in the same range and take those away. Every multiple of 12 is already a multiple of 3, so each one you remove really was on the first list.
Show the full solution
There are 60÷3=2060÷3=20 multiples of 3 from 3 through 60. Among them, 60÷12=560÷12=5 are multiples of 12, namely 12, 24, 36, 48 and 60. Striking those five out leaves 20−5=15.20−5=15​. Chaining runs downward only. Any n×12=(n×4)×3n×12=(n×4)×3 is a multiple of 3 and of 4, but a multiple of 3 such as 6 splits into 3s while falling short of a full bundle of 12.
Problem
A secret number is a multiple of 6, a perfect square, and lies between 100 and 400 inclusive. Find the sum of all possible values.
Show a hint
  • If a square k×kk×k is a multiple of 66, the side kk itself has to supply the factor 22 and the factor 33. What does that force kk to be a multiple of?
  • So every secret number is the square of a multiple of 66. Square 6,12,18,246,12,18,24 in turn, keep the ones that land between 100100 and 400400, and add those.
Show the full solution
122=144122=144 and 182=324182=324 are the only ones that qualify, and 144+324=468144+324=468. 468468​ A multiple of 6 carries a factor of 2 and a factor of 3, and in a square k×kk×k those can only come from kk itself, so kk is a multiple of 6 and the square is a multiple of 6×6=366×6=36. Squaring multiples of 6, 62=3662=36 sits below 100, 122=144122=144 and 182=324182=324 both land in range, and 242=576242=576 overshoots.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A school fits 40 lockers into one full rectangular block, every row the same length and no locker left over. Climb the factor pairs of 40 from 1×401×40 and stop once the two sides of a pair would cross. How many factors does 40 have in all?
Show the solution
Climb the pairs from 1 and let each small side fix its partner. 1×40,2×20,4×10,5×81×40,2×20,4×10,5×8 Reading both sides of every pair gives 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 401, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40, so 40 has 88​ factors. The numbers 3 and 6 do not divide 40, so they are skipped, and you stop after 6, because 7×7=497×7=49 already passes 40, so every factor above 6 is the partner of one you have. Four pairs with no side meeting itself gives an even count, exactly what a non-square should have.
Practice
A ring-toss scoreboard only ever adds 8 points per throw. Five friends claim scores of 24, 30, 48, 56, and 60. How many of these could the game actually show?
Show the solution
A score can appear only if it is a whole number of 8-point throws. Dividing, 24=8×324=8×3, 48=8×648=8×6, and 56=8×756=8×7 all come out clean, while 30 leaves a remainder of 6 and 60 leaves a remainder of 4. So 33​ of the five claimed scores are possible. Testing whether something is a multiple of 8 is just one division and a glance at the remainder.
Practice
Decide whether each claim about 61 is true or false. (a) 1 is a factor of 61. (b) 61 is a multiple of 61. (c) 0 is a multiple of 61. (d) 61 is a factor of 0. Enter your four verdicts in order.
Show the solution
(a) 61=1×6161=1×61, so 1 is a factor of 61. (b) 61=61×161=61×1, so 61 is a multiple of itself. (c) and (d) are the single line 0=61×00=61×0 read from its two ends, which makes 0 a multiple of 61 and 61 a factor of 0. All four hold, so the verdict is all four trueall four true​. The three facts behind this are that 1 divides every number, every number is a multiple of itself, and 0 is a multiple of everything.
Practice
Find the smallest and largest factors of 5656, then add them together.
Show the solution
The smallest factor of 5656 is 11 and the largest is 5656, so the sum is 1+561+56. 5757​ Nothing smaller than 11 divides a whole number evenly, so 11 sits at the bottom of every factor list. And a factor bigger than 5656 would need a partner smaller than 11 to multiply out to 5656, which no whole number does, so 5656 is its own largest factor. Every factor list is bookended the same way, 11 at the low end and the number itself at the high end.
Practice
Two bookends sit on every factor list. 11 is always the smallest factor, the single full-length row, and the number itself is always the largest, since no side of a rectangle can outrun its own area. So a factor of nn is always trapped between 11 and nn, which is why a factor hunt can never wander off forever.
Practice
Which of 72, 81, and 98 has an odd number of factors? Explain through self-pairing.
Show the solution
Of 72, 81, and 98, only 81=9×981=9×9 is a perfect square, since 8×8=648×8=64 and 10×10=10010×10=100 bracket the other two. So the odd factor count belongs to 8181​, whose factors are 1,3,9,27,811,3,9,27,81, five of them. Factors normally pair off as dd with n÷dn÷d, which makes the count even. Only a perfect square owns a factor that pairs with itself, and that lone factor tips the total to odd.
Practice
A ribbon is marked every 23 centimeters. What is the largest multiple of 23 below 500?
Show the solution
Fit as many whole 23-steps under the cap as possible. 500÷23=21 remainder 17500÷23=21 remainder 17 Those 21 steps land at 21×23=48321×23=483​, and the next mark, 22×23=50622×23=506, sails past 500. The greatest multiple of nn below a bound is the bound divided by nn with the remainder dropped, then multiplied back by nn.
Practice
A bakery packs rolls in trays of 26. What is the smallest three-digit multiple of 26?
Show the solution
A three-digit number is 100 or more, and 100÷26≈3.8100÷26≈3.8. You cannot bake 3.8 trays, so round up to 4 whole trays, giving 26×4=10426×4=104​. Rounding down to 3 would land at 78, still two digits. The smallest multiple of nn at or above a bound comes from dividing by nn and rounding the quotient up, then multiplying back.
Practice
Two-digit codes lit from inside are multiples of 6 whose digits sum to 6. How many codes light up?
Show the solution
Build the codes from the digit rule first, since it leaves the shorter list. The two-digit numbers whose digits sum to 6 are 15, 24, 33, 42, 51, 6015, 24, 33, 42, 51, 60, and no others, since a tens digit of 7 or more already overshoots. Each has digit sum 6, a multiple of 3, so each is divisible by 3 for free, and the only gate left is being even. That keeps 24, 42, and 60, so 33​ codes light up. When two rules overlap, start from whichever one produces the shorter list.
Practice
Find the largest three-digit multiple of 15 whose three digits are all different.
Show the solution
The greatest three-digit multiple of 15 is 990=15×66990=15×66, but its digits are 9, 9, 0 and the 9s repeat. Stepping down by 15 gives 975=15×65975=15×65, whose digits 9, 7, 5 are all different, so the answer is 975975​. Walking downward from the top means the first survivor you meet is the largest one, so you can stop the moment a candidate passes.
Practice
An amphitheater has 7 rows with 14, 28, 42, … seats. Find the total number of seats.
Show the solution
The seven rows hold 14,28,42,56,70,84,9814,28,42,56,70,84,98, which is 14×114×1 through 14×714×7. Pull the shared 14 out front. 14×(1+2+3+4+5+6+7)=14×28=39214×(1+2+3+4+5+6+7)=14×28=392​ Pairing from the ends makes the inner sum quick, 1+7=81+7=8, 2+6=82+6=8, 3+5=83+5=8, plus the middle 4, so 3×8+4=283×8+4=28. When every term shares a common step, factor that step out and add only the small counting numbers left.
Practice
A runner claps at every 13th metre. How many claps fall strictly between metres 150 and 850?
Show the solution
The claps sit at the multiples of 13. The largest one strictly under 850 is 845=13×65845=13×65, since 13×66=85813×66=858 overshoots, so 65 multiples sit below the top. The largest at or below 150 is 143=13×11143=13×11, so 11 sit below the window. Subtracting, 65−11=5465−11=54​ Neither 150 nor 850 is a multiple of 13, so the word strictly costs nothing here. Count up to the top, subtract what falls below the bottom, and always check whether an endpoint is itself a multiple.
Practice
Two trucks each carry a multiple of 15 apples. Show 400 is impossible, then find the nearest reachable total.
Show the solution
Two multiples of 15 add to 15a+15b=15(a+b)15a+15b=15(a+b), still a multiple of 15. But 15×26=39015×26=390 and 15×27=40515×27=405, so 400 sits strictly between two multiples and is not one, which makes the claimed total impossible. Of those two neighbours, 405 is only 5 away while 390 is 10 away, and 405 is reachable as 15+39015+390, so the nearest total is 405405​. Once a target fails the membership test for a closed set, the best you can do is the nearest member to it.
Practice
A bead artist works only in kits of 24. For each of 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, and 16, decide whether the bead count must be a multiple of that number. How many of the six are guaranteed?
Show the solution
The factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 241, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Of the six sizes asked about, 2, 3, 4, and 8 are on that list, so a bead count of 24×k24×k must be a multiple of each of them, giving 44​ guaranteed. Neither 9 nor 16 divides 24, and 24 itself is the counterexample for both. Being a multiple of nn only forces divisibility by the factors of nn, so the inheritance chains downward and stops there.
Practice
Find every perfect square that is a multiple of 45 and stays below 2000. How many such numbers are there?
Show the solution
Since 45=32×545=32×5, a square multiple of 45 needs a factor of 5, and a prime can only get into s×ss×s by living in ss, so ss carries a 5 and likewise a 3. That makes ss a multiple of 15 and the square a multiple of 152=225152=225. Squaring, 152=225152=225 and 302=900302=900 stay under 2000, while 452=2025452=2025 overshoots, so there are 22​ such numbers. A perfect square needs every prime to an even power, which rounds the requirement up from 45 to 225.
Practice
A perfect number equals the sum of its proper factors: 1+2+3=61+2+3=6 and 1+2+4+7+14=281+2+4+7+14=28. They are rare, and no one has ever found an odd perfect number or proved none exists.

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
